engagement.model: Human eosinophils and Th2 cells in vitro
engagement.note: AZD1981 blocked PGD2-driven shape change and chemotaxis of human eosinophils and Th2 cells; the class was profiled in these assays.
engagement.quote: AZD1981 inhibited DP2 -mediated shape change and CD11b up-regulation in human eosinophils, shape change in basophils and chemotaxis of human eosinophils and Th2 cells with similar potency.
engagement.judgement: Opens the strip with a member drug (AZD1981); fevipiprant and QAV680 were profiled in the same human eosinophil/Th2 assays (Sandham 2013, 2017). Non-member ramatroban (Sugimoto 2003) used the assay earlier and is not scored. epub_year 2012 inferred from the PMID's assignment date (print April 2013).

engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading; NCT01545726 posted no results.
engagement.model: Human eosinophils and Th2 cells in vitro
engagement.note: Fevipiprant 225 mg twice daily cut sputum eosinophils 3.5-fold more than placebo over 12 weeks in 61 eosinophilic asthmatics.
engagement.quote: Compared with baseline, mean sputum eosinophil percentage was reduced by 4·5 times in the fevipiprant group and by 1·3 times in the placebo group (difference between groups 3·5 times, 95% CI 1·7-7·0; p=0·0014).
engagement.reason: Patient airway eosinophils fell as predicted
engagement.judgement: Paired comparison: the in-vitro model predicts blocked eosinophil recruitment, and sputum eosinophils are a downstream readout of it. No member reported ex-vivo whole-blood shape change in dosed humans in an abstract I could read, so no direct-tier entry. MK-1029 allergen-challenge sputum eosinophil data (NCT01343407, results 2019-02-08) are later and were not read.

dose.model: Human eosinophil DP2 potency scaled to human exposure
dose.note: In-vitro potency on human eosinophils set the exposure the class aimed for in humans.
dose.quote: AZD1981 is a DP2 antagonist that blocks functional responses in eosinophils, Th2 cells and basophils. It exhibited similar potency irrespective of the cell type, DP2 agonist or species used.
dose.judgement: Opening entry for the occupancy model; no member published a quantitative human occupancy target in an abstract.

dose.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading; the abstract gives no occupancy number, so magnitude is direction_only.
dose.model: Human eosinophil DP2 potency scaled to human exposure
dose.note: Fevipiprant plasma levels in healthy volunteers reached the occupancy the in-vitro pharmacology called for, and were tolerated to 500 mg/day.
dose.quote: Systemic concentrations were sufficiently high to achieve relevant target occupancy, considering in vitro pharmacology data.
dose.judgement: Scored same, not untested: the source itself states the target was reached, and the doses that reached it then moved sputum eosinophils (Gonem 2016) and met the FEV1 primary in dose-ranging (Bateman 2017, 150 mg/day optimum). margin_stated false: the tolerated range is human data, not a model-stated margin.

dose.model: Human eosinophil DP2 potency scaled to human exposure
dose.note: At 150 and 450 mg, both at or above target exposure, fevipiprant did not significantly cut exacerbations in 1,771 severe asthmatics; development stopped.

dose.judgement: Decision table row 'reached, failed, abandoned': dose contra derived from efficacy so the failure is counted once. Year is the LUSTER-1 registry posting (NCT02555683, 2020-05-18); ZEAL-1 (NCT03215758, FEV1 primary) posted results 2020-02-12, same year. A Novartis press release in late 2019 likely announced the misses; not verified, so not used for dating.

efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading; the abstract does not name the species or readouts.
efficacy.note: QAV680, a member, was effective in rodent CRTh2-dependent mechanistic and allergic disease models before entering asthma trials.
efficacy.short: QAV680 effective in rodent allergy models
efficacy.quote: The molecule exhibited good oral bioavailability in the rat, combined with efficacy in rodent CRTh2-dependent mechanistic and allergic disease models and was suitable for clinical development.
efficacy.judgement: model_first_use_year 2009 is a proxy: QAV680 entered asthma trials (NCT00814216, completed 2009-10) on these data, published only in 2013. AZD1981 could not be tested in mouse or rat cells, which did not respond to DP2 agonists (Schmidt 2013), so the rodent model's relevance is itself doubtful.

efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading. The rodent model was run on QAV680, not AZD1981.
efficacy.note: AZD1981 up to 400 mg twice daily added to ICS/LABA did not improve FEV1 in 1,140 atopic asthmatics; results posted September 2013.
efficacy.quote: However, the improvement for the highest AZD1981 dose (400 mg BID) vs placebo was not statistically significant (0.02 L, P=0.58), preventing interpretation of statistical testing for the lower doses.
efficacy.judgement: Dated to the registry posting of NCT01197794 (2013-09-10), the first public in-class primary-endpoint result. Later member trials split: BI 671800 met its FEV1 primary (Hall 2015, +3-4% predicted) and fevipiprant met it in dose-ranging (Bateman 2017), but a failed model stays failed and one drug's contra beats another's same. Phase 3 confirmed the miss (LUSTER, ZEAL).

patient_trials.quote: Following 4 weeks of treatment, there was a nonsignificant increase in morning peak expiratory flow on AZD1981 1,000 mg bid (9.5 L/min vs placebo, P=0.086 [study 1] and 12 L/min vs placebo, P=0.16 [study 2]).
These findings suggest that BI 671800 is associated with a small improvement in FEV1 in symptomatic controller-naïve asthma patients, and in patients on ICS.
There were no significant differences between QAW039 and placebo for trough forced expiratory volume in 1 s (FEV1) or Asthma control questionnaire (ACQ) in the total population.

Fevipiprant produced a statistically significant improvement in the primary end-point of change in pre-dose forced expiratory volume in 1 s at week 12 (p=0.0035) with a maximum model-averaged difference to placebo of 0.112 L.

Although neither trial showed a statistically significant reduction in asthma exacerbations after adjusting for multiple testing, consistent and modest reductions in exacerbations rates were observed in both studies with the 450 mg dose of fevipiprant.
Although GB001 did not significantly reduce the odds of asthma worsening, reductions favoring GB001 were observed.

efficacy.judgement: A different model, run after LUSTER, that the authors set beside the human trials; scored retro, not same (decision 10). product_in_model null because the abstract does not name the antagonist.

efficacy.note: Setipiprant cut the allergen late asthmatic response 25.6%, predicting a lung-function benefit; AZD1981, a member, had already missed its FEV1 primary in 1,140 asthmatics.
efficacy.short: Challenge said yes; FEV1 trials missed

efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading of both papers. Model side: Diamant 2014 (PMID 24964348, entrez 2014-06-26): 'setipiprant significantly reduced the allergen-induced late asthmatic response (LAR), inhibiting the area under the response vs. time curve (AUC(3-10 h)) by on average 25.6% (P = 0.006)'. AZD1981 was never run in the challenge model.
efficacy.reason: Challenge positive, member FEV1 trials failed
efficacy.judgement: Paired, not stated: no source sets the challenge result beside a member's trial. Dated 2014, when the model side became public (the AZD1981 registry result was posted 2013-09-10). Sibling-drug pairing as in the main strip. MK-1029's own challenge (NCT01343407, posted 2019-02-08) cut LAR FEV1 AUC to 0.48x placebo; its phase 2 FEV1 primaries split (NCT02720081 +0.107 L, p=0.023; NCT01624974 +0.047 L, p=0.28) and the program stopped. Not scored neg: no source states a class LAR bar.

safety.model: Off-target selectivity panels; animal toxicology unpublished
safety.note: AZD1981 was clean on over 340 enzymes and receptors; no member's animal toxicology or regulatory review is public.
safety.short: Clean selectivity panel; tox never public
safety.quote: Binding was reversible, non-competitive and highly selective against a panel of more than 340 other enzymes and receptors, including DP1 (>1000-fold selective).
safety.judgement: No member was filed with FDA or EMA (manifest: no NDA/BLA), so no review names the toxicology package. Patient safety was placebo-like for fevipiprant (LUSTER serious AEs 9% in every arm), but GB001 60 mg carried a risk of liver injury (Moss 2022). With no public GB001 preclinical toxicology I cannot say whether the model was silent or stated a margin, so the hepatic signal is left unscored rather than called contra.
